s1.syndrome_frame: persistent unilateral breast swelling with a new subareolar mass
salient_findings: persistent swelling of the left breast for four years
new, mildly tender, firm 1-cm subareolar mass under the left nipple
lobulated retroareolar mass approximately 1.5 cm in diameter on mammography
key_facts: persistent swelling of the left breast for four years
new, mildly tender, firm 1-cm subareolar mass under the left nipple
repeat ultrasonography demonstrates a 1.5-cm long, solid structure with lobular architecture
mammography reveals a lobulated retroareolar mass approximately 1.5 cm in diameter

shortlist.label: Gynecomastia
shortlist.why_kept: Initial diagnosis and persistent unilateral breast swelling

shortlist.label: Male Breast Cancer
shortlist.why_kept: New, mildly tender, firm subareolar mass and solid structure on ultrasonography

shortlist.label: Intraductal Papilloma
shortlist.why_kept: Lobular architecture on ultrasonography and lobulated retroareolar mass on mammography

shortlist.label: Fibroadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Solid structure with lobular architecture and BIRADS III classification

shortlist.label: Adenocarcinoma of the breast
shortlist.why_kept: New subareolar mass and lobulated retroareolar mass on mammography

raw.rationale: new, mildly tender, firm 1-cm subareolar mass and a solid structure with lobular architecture on ultrasonography, along with a lobulated retroareolar mass on mammography, are concerning features for malignancy

rejected.label: Gynecomastia
rejected.why: initial diagnosis, but new mass and solidity on imaging suggest a different etiology

rejected.label: Intraductal Papilloma
rejected.why: typically presents with nipple discharge, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Fibroadenoma
rejected.why: usually a well-circumscribed, mobile mass, which does not match the description of the firm, mildly tender mass in this case

rejected.label: Adenocarcinoma of the breast
rejected.why: essentially the same diagnosis as Male Breast Cancer, but the latter is more specific to the patient's sex
